name: 红土坡
Red Earth Slope
before: 一面山坡红得像刚宰了牛，坡上的土抓一把能把手染红。一伙窑霸占了这面坡，挖红土烧砖，挖得坡上全是大坑，烧出来的砖卖到四乡。坡下一个白胡子老头挑着空颜料担子，跟窑霸们磨了三天嘴皮，只想要一小筐最红的土，被一脚踹了回来。

A hillside as red as a fresh-butchered ox: grab a handful of earth and it stains your hand. A gang of kiln bosses has taken the slope, digging the red earth for bricks, riddling it with pits and selling the bricks across the district. At the bottom, a white-bearded old man with empty paint baskets on a carrying pole has argued with them for three days for one small basket of the reddest earth, and been kicked back down for his pains.
after: 窑霸被赶跑，老头跪在坡上挑土，挑一捧，捻一捻。他说土红是含铁的土，铁一锈就红，最正的那一层，抹在脸颊上像喝了酒。他报了名字：吴半壁，半壁村的画匠，要把千佛洞里被刮掉的三百张脸补回来，「红有了，还差绿、差白」。他抱着那筐土，跟着你们走了。

The kiln bosses chased off, the old man kneels on the slope sorting earth: a handful, rub it between his fingers. Red earth is earth with iron in it, he says; iron rusts red, and the truest layer, on a cheek, looks like a man who's had a drink. He gives his name: Wu Banbi, the painter of Half Wall village. He means to restore the three hundred faces scraped from the caves. 'I've got the red. I still need green, and white.' Hugging his basket of earth, he comes along with you.

name: 赌凿坊
The Chisel Den
before: 山脚一间石屋里吆五喝六，一群石匠围着桌子赌骰子，押的是自己的凿子。坐庄的是几个外地来的老千，骰子灌了铅，石匠们输得只剩一双手。门口站着老千雇的打手，谁想把凿子赎回去，就先挨一顿揍。

A stone hut at the foot of the hill rings with shouting: a crowd of stonemasons playing dice, staking their own chisels. The bank is run by card sharps from out of town with loaded dice, and the masons have lost everything but their hands. The sharps' hired muscle stands at the door, and anyone who wants to buy back his chisel gets a beating first.
after: 老千和打手被撵走，凿子物归原主。石匠们臊得满脸通红，说他们都是老凿的徒弟，师父病了大半年，没人管着，就学坏了。那年冬天千里号三百人跟着师父学凿崖，「师父说，三百个门外汉，干出了三百个匠人的活」。老凿住在山脚最里头的死胡同里。

The sharps and their muscle thrown out, every chisel goes back to its owner. The masons blush scarlet. They're all Lao Zao's apprentices; the master's been ill for half a year and with no one keeping them in line they went bad. That winter the Qianli three hundred learned to work the cliff from him. 'Master said three hundred amateurs did the work of three hundred masons.' Lao Zao lives at the very end of the dead end at the foot of the hill.

name: 栈道口
Walkway Gate
before: 通往断崖栈道的路口筑了一道石门，金面卫最硬的一队守在这里，刀卫堵门，弩手上了崖，骑卫在门外来回巡。他们守的不是外敌：门内的栈道上住着一个人，洞主有令，他不下来，别人也不许上去。门楣上有人用炭画了一只小骆驼。

A stone gate has been built across the way to the broken-cliff walkway, held by the toughest troop of Gold Masks: swordsmen in the gateway, crossbowmen up on the rock, riders patrolling outside. They aren't guarding against outsiders. A man lives on the walkway beyond, and by the Lord's order he doesn't come down and nobody goes up. On the lintel someone has drawn a little camel in charcoal.
after: 金面卫让开了石门，你们抬头往上看：崖腰的栈道断成了好几截，最高的一截上站着一个拄拐的汉子，身边卧着一峰瘸腿的老骆驼。他看见你们的旗子，愣了好半天，扯着嗓子往下喊：「打的什么旗？走近点，让我看清楚！」

The Gold Masks give way and you look up. The walkway on the cliff's waist is broken into several stretches, and on the highest one stands a man on a crutch with an old lame camel lying beside him. He sees your banner and stands stunned a long moment, then bellows down: 'What flag is that? Come closer, let me see it properly!'

name: 漂木湾
Driftwood Bend
before: 宕泉河在这里拐了个弯，上游漂下来的木头都卡在湾里。最近漂下来的是一批削好的榆木梁，一伙河霸用长钩子把木头全捞上岸，说是「河里的东西谁捞归谁」，正劈了当柴烧。湾边一个放木排的老汉急得直拍大腿：「那是给栈道上送的！」

The Dangquan river bends here, and timber floating down from upstream jams in the bend. The latest arrivals are squared elm beams, and a gang of river bullies has hooked them all ashore: 'What's in the river belongs to whoever catches it.' They're splitting them for firewood. An old raftsman on the bank slaps his thighs in despair: 'Those are for the walkway!'
after: 河霸被赶下河去，老汉把剩下的木梁捆成排。每根梁上都刻着几个字：「送栈道，交曹。」老汉说这木头是洞主出钱买的，年年秋天从上游放一批下来，栈道上那人拿去修栈，十年没断过。「洞主那人，」老汉说，「对活人凶，对木头好。」

The bullies driven into the river, the old man lashes the remaining beams into a raft. Each is carved: 'For the walkway. Deliver to Cao.' The Lord pays for this timber, the raftsman says, and every autumn a batch is floated down from upstream for the man on the walkway to mend it with. Ten years, never missed. 'The Lord,' he says, 'is hard on the living and kind to timber.'

name: 牵驼坡
Camel Thieves' Slope
before: 山坡上一大伙偷骆驼的贼，步、弩、骑都有，围着一峰瘸了腿的老骆驼，又拽缰绳又抽鞭子。那骆驼每天下崖到河边喝水，喝完自己再爬回栈道，今天被他们堵住了。老骆驼四蹄钉在地上，冲着贼头喷了一脸口水。

A big gang of camel thieves, foot, crossbow and horse, surrounds an old lame camel on the slope, hauling at its halter and whipping it. Every day the camel comes down the cliff to drink at the river and climbs back up to the walkway on its own; today they've cornered it. The old camel plants all four feet and spits a faceful into the chief thief's eyes.
after: 偷驼贼被打跑，老骆驼甩了甩脖子，慢吞吞地往崖上走，你们跟在后面。它的鞍子上烙着一个「千」字，缰绳上拴着一只小木牌：「老黄，千里号驼队。腿瘸，留山，与曹三作伴。」崖规牌上那条「看见骆驼给它让路」，说的就是它。

The thieves chased off, the old camel shakes its neck and plods back up the cliff with you behind it. Its saddle is branded with the character Qian, and on its halter hangs a little wooden tag: 'Lao Huang. Qianli camel train. Lame, stays on the mountain to keep Cao San company.' The rule on the cliff board, 'give way to the camel', means him.

name: 铜绿洞
The Verdigris Mine
before: 吴半壁要找绿，领着你们来到一座废弃的铜矿，矿洞口的石头上一片片绿斑和蓝斑，像长了苔。一伙散了伙的矿工占了矿洞，步、弩、骑凑了一大帮，在这儿剪径。吴半壁一看见洞壁上的颜色，眼睛就直了，差点自己冲进去。

Wu Banbi needs green, and he leads you to an abandoned copper mine whose entrance rocks are blotched green and blue as if with moss. A band of miners whose crew broke up has taken it over, foot, crossbow and horse, and robs travellers from here. At the sight of the colours on the walls Wu's eyes go wide, and he nearly charges in by himself.
after: 矿工们被打散，吴半壁扑到洞壁上一块块地敲：「石绿和石青常长在一处，都是铜矿露出地面，叫水和气慢慢锈出来的，一个绿，一个蓝，亲兄弟。」他敲了满满两袋，绿的画衣裳，蓝的画天。「千里号的人那年穿的是青衣绿袍，这回颜色对得上了。」

The miners scattered, Wu throws himself at the wall and chips away. 'Malachite and azurite grow side by side. Both come from copper ore near the surface, slowly rusted out by water and air. One green, one blue, brothers.' He fills two bags: green for robes, blue for sky. 'The Qianli people wore blue coats and green robes that year. This time the colours will match.'

name: 断崖栈道
The Broken Cliff Walkway
before: 你们攀上栈道，一截一截往上走，木梁在脚下咯吱响。最高那截栈道上，拄拐的汉子把一块铜牌高高举过头顶，牌上铸着「千里号·驼」四个字。可栈道另一头摸上来一伙盗经贼，他们想借这条栈道爬进上层的窟里偷经，嫌这个瘸子挡路，正拿刀砍他身后的栈道梁。

You climb the walkway stretch by stretch, beams creaking underfoot. On the highest section the man on the crutch holds a bronze token high over his head, cast with the words 'Qianli Caravan: Camel Train'. But from the far end a band of sutra thieves has crept up; they want to use the walkway to get into the upper caves and steal sutras, and since the cripple's in their way they're hacking at the beams behind him.
after: 盗经贼被打下了崖，汉子放下铜牌：他就是曹三。那年冬天修栈道，他摔断了腿，商队开春要走，账房把驼队的令牌塞给他：「留下的也是千里号的人。」他就在崖上住下了，夜里补崖，一补十年。他问：「他们回来了没有？」你们摇头。曹三点点头：「那我再补一年。」

With the thieves knocked off the cliff, the man lowers the token. He is Cao San. That winter, building the walkway, he fell and broke his leg. When the caravan left in spring, the bookkeeper pressed the camel train's token into his hand: 'Those who stay behind are Qianli too.' So he settled on the cliff and has mended it by night for ten years. He studies your banner and asks, 'Are they back yet?' You shake your heads. Cao San nods. 'Then I'll patch for another year.'

name: 老凿洞
Old Chisel's Cave
before: 山脚死胡同的最里头，一个小窟就是老凿的家，窟里堆满了大大小小的凿子、锤子和墨斗。老凿病在炕上，咳得直不起腰。一伙关内来的包工头带着打手堵在窟口，逼他在一张契上按手印，把他的「手令」卖给他们：这一带的匠人只认老凿的手令，有了它，就能使唤所有的匠人。

At the very back of the dead end at the foot of the hill, a small cave is Lao Zao's home, crammed with chisels, hammers and chalk lines of every size. The old man lies sick on his platform bed, coughing double. Contractors from inside the Pass have blocked the entrance with their bullies, pushing him to put his thumbprint on a contract selling them his hand order. Every mason in these parts obeys Lao Zao's hand order; whoever holds it can command them all.
after: 包工头被打跑，老凿撑着坐起来，从炕席底下摸出一块木牌，牌上是他亲手刻的令：「急工。见令者，昼夜不歇，一日抵三日。」那年冬天，北崖一块悬岩裂了缝，底下就是刚画好的千里窟，他写了这道令，匠人和千里号三百人举着火把干了一天一夜，把悬岩撑住了。「这是营造加速令，」他把木牌交给你们，「拿到工地上一亮，匠人们就知道是急活，一天能干完好几天的工。」他又咳了几声：「那三百个人走的时候，说回来还跟我干活。我等着。」

The contractors chased off, Lao Zao props himself up and draws a wooden tablet from under his mat, an order carved in his own hand: 'Urgent work. All who see this order work day and night without rest; one day counts for three.' That winter an overhang on the north cliff cracked, right above the newly painted Qianli Cave. He wrote this order, and the masons and the three hundred worked a day and a night by torchlight and shored it up. 'This is the Building Hand Order,' he says, giving it to you. 'Show it on any site and the masons know it's a rush job. They'll do several days' work in one.' He coughs again. 'When those three hundred left, they said they'd come back and work for me again. I'm waiting.'

name: 匠人滩
Masons' Strand
before: 河滩上搭着一片匠人的窝棚，晒着草帽和裹腿。一伙盗经贼摸了过来，拿刀逼匠人们给他们打一条地道，从河滩一直通到一座封了门的窟里去。匠人们抱着凿子不肯动，盗经贼就一个一个地往河里扔，已经扔下去三个了。

Masons' shacks crowd the riverbank, straw hats and puttees drying in the sun. A band of sutra thieves has crept in and is forcing them at knifepoint to dig a tunnel from the strand right into a sealed cave. The masons cling to their chisels and won't budge, so the thieves are throwing them in the river one at a time. Three have gone in already.
after: 盗经贼被打跑，掉进河的三个也爬了上来，冻得直打哆嗦。匠头说：「老凿教的，崖上不许乱打洞，一个洞就是一道伤。」他们说千里号的人当年也这么守过规矩，账房还把规矩抄了三百份，每人揣一份，「走的时候说，到了别的地方也照着办」。

The thieves chased off, the three who went in the river climb out shivering. 'Lao Zao taught us,' their foreman says. 'No digging holes in the cliff at random. Every hole is a wound.' The Qianli caravan kept the same rule back then, they tell you. The bookkeeper even copied it out three hundred times so each of them carried one. 'When they left, they said they'd keep it wherever they went.'

name: 白土窑
White Earth Kilns
before: 一片白花花的土坡，坡下几座石灰窑，烧窑的人从这里挖白土、烧石灰，供崖上抹墙用。一伙窑痞赶走了窑工，把窑口一封，石灰卖出天价，崖上补墙的泥都和不起来。吴半壁蹲在坡下，捏起一撮白土对着太阳看：「画脸的底子，就是它。」

A slope of dazzling white earth with a few lime kilns below it, where kiln men dig white clay and burn lime for plastering the cliff. A gang of kiln thugs has driven the workers off, sealed the kilns and sold lime at sky-high prices, so no one on the cliff can mix plaster. Wu Banbi squats at the foot of the slope, holding a pinch of white earth up to the sun. 'This is the ground for a face.'
after: 窑痞被赶走，窑工们回来了，窑口又冒起白烟，一车车石灰往崖上送。吴半壁挖了满满一袋最细的白土，三样颜色凑齐了。他把袋子挨个摸了一遍：「只差金。」窑工头说那年千里号的人也来这里背过石灰，背一筐唱一句，唱一整天不重样。

The thugs gone, the kiln men come back, white smoke rises again and lime goes up to the cliff by the cartload. Wu Banbi digs a bag of the finest white earth, and now he has all three colours. He pats each bag in turn. 'Only the gold is missing.' The kiln foreman says the Qianli caravan carried lime from here that year, a song for every basket, a whole day without repeating one.
first: 窑痞的棚子里抄出三十车石灰、五车木炭、一窖腌咸鱼、十几把抢来的瓦刀，还有一摞写好的「石灰欠条」，连崖上那个瘸子都欠了他们两筐。

The thugs' shed holds thirty cartloads of lime, five of charcoal, a cellar of salted fish, a dozen stolen trowels, and a stack of lime IOUs written out in advance; even the cripple on the cliff owes them two baskets.
pass: 每次路过，窑工们都从窑壁上揭下几张烤得焦黄的面饼，饼底还带着石头的纹路，再给你们的车上捎两筐石灰：「营里要补墙，用得着。」

Every time you pass, the kiln men peel a few flatbreads baked golden on the kiln wall, the stone's pattern still on their undersides, and load two baskets of lime onto your cart. 'Your camp'll have walls to patch. You'll need it.'

name: 凿子林
Chisel Grove
before: 死胡同尽头的一块大石上插着密密麻麻的铁凿，远看像一片光秃秃的小树林。一伙收铁的雇佣兵盯上了这些凿子，步、弩、骑三路守在石头边，正一根根往外拔，说熔了能打三百把刀。可凿子插得太深，拔了半天，才拔出来十几根。

On a big boulder at the end of a dead end, iron chisels stand so thick they look from afar like a grove of bare saplings. Mercenaries buying up iron have their eyes on them and hold the boulder with foot, crossbow and horse, pulling the chisels out one by one: melt them down and they'll make three hundred swords. But they're driven in deep, and after all this time only a dozen are out.
after: 雇佣兵被打退，你们把凿子一根根插了回去。每根木柄上都刻着名字，凿头磨得只剩半截。匠人们说，这是千里号三百人的凿子，开春走的时候一人一根插在这块石头上，「说是借老凿的手艺，回来再拿。凿子在，手艺就在」。三百根，一根不少。

The mercenaries beaten back, you drive the chisels back in one by one. Each wooden handle is carved with a name, and the blades are worn down to half their length. These are the Qianli three hundred's chisels, the masons say. When they left in spring each man drove his into this boulder. 'They said they'd borrowed Lao Zao's craft and would collect it when they came back. While the chisels are here, so is the craft.' Three hundred, not one missing.

name: 河边草场
Riverside Fodder Yard
before: 河边一座草料场，码着一垛垛干草和苜蓿，是千佛洞来往驼马吃草的地方。一伙兵痞霸了草场，马料一斤卖一钱，香客的驴饿得啃门框。看草场的老汉被他们赶去喂猪，他的两个孙子躲在草垛里，大气不敢出。

A fodder yard by the river, stacked with hay and alfalfa, where the camels and horses coming to the caves are fed. Soldier-thugs have seized it and sell fodder at a coin a pound; the pilgrims' donkeys are so hungry they gnaw the door frames. The old yard keeper has been sent to feed the pigs, and his two grandsons hide in a haystack, scarcely daring to breathe.
after: 兵痞被赶走，老汉的两个孙子从草垛里钻出来，头上全是草。老汉说，栈道上那峰叫老黄的老骆驼，每年冬天他都给它留一垛最好的苜蓿，是洞主吩咐的。「洞主说，人可以饿，那峰骆驼不能饿，那是千里号的骆驼。」

The thugs chased off, the old man's grandsons wriggle out of the haystack, straw all over their heads. Every winter, the old man says, he keeps the best stack of alfalfa for Lao Huang, the old camel on the walkway, on the Lord's orders. 'The Lord says people can go hungry, but that camel mustn't. It's a Qianli camel.'
first: 草场里抄出兵痞们囤的六百捆干草、三十袋豆料、二十条驼毛毡子，还有一匹偷来的枣红马，老汉一眼认出是邻村的，牵回去还了。

From the yard you recover six hundred bales of hay hoarded by the thugs, thirty sacks of bean fodder, twenty camel-hair blankets, and a stolen chestnut horse that the old man recognises as a neighbour's and leads home.
pass: 每次路过，老汉的两个孙子都抢着把你们的马牵到河边饮水，刷毛、编鬃，临走往鞍袋里塞一包炒黄豆：「人吃一半，马吃一半。」

Every time you pass, the old man's grandsons fight over leading your horses to the river to drink, brushing their coats and braiding their manes, and as you leave they stuff a bag of roasted soybeans into your saddlebags. 'Half for you, half for the horses.'

name: 送粮渡
Supply Ferry
before: 河边一处小渡口，每隔几天，金面卫就从这里撑船往上游的崖下送东西：粮、木料、灯油、给老黄的苜蓿。今天船刚靠岸，一伙河匪就从芦苇里冲了出来，把船上的东西往自己筏子上搬。撑船的金面卫只有两个，拿着篙子左支右挡。

At a little ferry by the river, every few days the Gold Masks pole a boat upstream to the foot of the cliff with supplies: grain, timber, lamp oil, alfalfa for Lao Huang. Today the boat has barely touched the bank when river bandits burst out of the reeds and start hauling the cargo onto their own rafts. There are only two Gold Masks poling, fending them off with their poles.
after: 河匪被赶散，撑船的金面卫摘下面具擦汗，是个年轻人。他从船舱里取出一块铜牌递给你们，是曹三托他捎下来的，正是那块「千里号·驼」。曹三带话说：「我走不了，牌子替我走。拿给洞主看，他认这块牌。告诉他，栈道我守得住，叫他也别守得太苦。」

The bandits scattered, one of the boatmen takes off his mask to wipe his sweat. He's a young man. From the hold he brings out a bronze token and hands it to you: Cao San sent it down with him, the very 'Qianli Caravan: Camel Train'. Cao San's message: 'I can't go, so the token will go for me. Show it to the Lord, he knows it. Tell him I can hold the walkway, and he needn't keep his own watch so hard.'

name: 山门坡
Temple Gate Slope
before: 上山门的石阶下坐着一个熟人：了账和尚，毛驴拴在一边，驴背上还驮着那两箱债簿。他回寺里来，却被一队金面刀卫拦在山门外，进不去。刀卫说：「洞主有令，出了山门的和尚不许回来。」了账急得跳脚：「我是这寺里的和尚！我师父就是你们洞主！」

At the foot of the steps up to the temple gate sits a familiar face: Liaozhang the monk, his donkey tethered beside him, still carrying the two chests of debt books. He's come home to the temple, but a troop of Gold Mask swordsmen has stopped him outside the gate. 'The Lord's orders: monks who've left the gate don't come back.' Liaozhang is hopping mad. 'I'm a monk of this temple! My master is your Lord!'
after: 刀卫们被打退了，了账拍着身上的土说：他师父法号无相，原是寺里管窟的和尚。七年前三百张脸被刮的那一夜，师父脱了袈裟，戴上金面，从此闭山，谁都不见，连他也不见。「师父欠我一个说法，千里号欠寺里一笔账，」他说，「沙海里说好的，账一起对。」

The swordsmen beaten back, Liaozhang brushes himself down and explains. His master's monastic name is Wuxiang, 'Without Form'; he was the temple's keeper of the caves. Seven years ago, the night the three hundred faces were scraped, his master took off his robe, put on the golden mask and closed the mountain, and since then sees no one, not even him. 'My master owes me an explanation and the Qianli caravan owes the temple a debt,' he says. 'We agreed in the Sand Sea: we settle the accounts together.'

name: 挂镜林
Mirror Wood
before: 胡杨林里一闪一闪的，树杈上挂着一面面铜镜，大的像锅盖，小的像巴掌。一队金面弩手守在林子里，拿镜子对着太阳往山上晃，一晃一停，是在给崖上报信：有人来了。他们看见了你们，镜子晃得更急了，弩也抬了起来。

Flashes wink through the poplar wood: bronze mirrors hang in the branches, some the size of pot lids, some palm-sized. A troop of Gold Mask crossbowmen in the wood is angling them at the sun and flashing toward the mountain, flash and pause, signalling up the cliff that someone's coming. Spotting you, they flash faster and raise their crossbows.
after: 弩手们退走了，了账摘下一面小镜子，翻过来看背面的铭文：「粟特康氏造」。「这是千里号送来的那一车镜子，」他说，「本来是给窟里引光照壁画的，师父拿它们报信了。」他把镜子揣进怀里：「留着，说不定用得上。」

The crossbowmen withdraw. Liaozhang takes down a small mirror and turns it over to read the inscription: 'Made by the Kang family of Sogdiana.' 'This is that cartload of mirrors the Qianli caravan brought,' he says. 'They were meant to bounce light into the caves so people could see the murals. Master's been using them for signals.' He tucks it into his robe. 'I'll keep it. It may come in handy.'

name: 油驼道
Oil Camel Road
before: 路边卧着一排骆驼，每峰驮着两只油罐，赶驼的是个十来岁的小马贼，一脸的沙。一伙盗油贼围着驼队，正把油罐一只只卸下来：灯油金贵，一罐能换一头羊。小马贼抱着一只罐子不撒手，喊着：「这是王给千佛洞的！」

A string of camels kneels by the road, two oil jars slung on each. Their driver is a bandit boy of ten or so, his face caked in sand. A gang of oil thieves surrounds the train, unloading the jars one by one: lamp oil is precious, a jar will buy a sheep. The boy clings to one jar and won't let go, shouting, 'This is the King's, for the caves!'
after: 盗油贼被打跑，小马贼抹了一把鼻涕。每只油罐的封泥上都按着一个歪歪扭扭的「王」字，了账一眼就认了出来：沙海里那个替千里号还了十年灯油的王。小马贼说王今年腿疼，走不动了，派他送来，「王说，送到灯跟前，看着它点上，再回去」。

The oil thieves chased off, the boy wipes his nose. Every jar's clay seal is pressed with a lopsided character, King. Liaozhang knows it at once: the King of the Sand Sea, who paid ten years of the Qianli caravan's lamp oil. The King's leg hurts this year and he couldn't travel, the boy says, so he sent him. 'The King said deliver it to the lamp, watch it lit, then come home.'

name: 守灯径
Lamp Keeper's Path
before: 一条小径通往山脚的一座老禅房，禅房里住着寺里最老的和尚，人称灯公。一队金面刀卫守着小径，洞主有令，谁也不许打扰灯公。可小马贼的油要送到灯跟前，了账的话要说给灯公听，刀卫们一步不让：「灯公病了，见不得人。」

A path leads to an old meditation hut at the foot of the hill, home of the temple's oldest monk, called the Lamp Elder. A troop of Gold Mask swordsmen guards the path: by the Lord's orders, the Lamp Elder is not to be disturbed. But the bandit boy's oil must be delivered to the lamp, and Liaozhang has things to say to the Elder. The guards won't give an inch. 'The Elder is ill. He can't see anyone.'
after: 刀卫们被打退，领头的叹了口气：「灯公这几天天天问一句：沙海那边，来人了没有？我们不敢答。」了账一听，眼圈就红了：灯公是他师父的师父，十年前借给千里号灯油的就是他。刀卫让开了路，说：「进去吧。他等的就是你们。」

The swordsmen beaten back, their leader sighs. 'Every day lately the Elder asks: has anyone come from the Sand Sea? We didn't dare answer.' Liaozhang's eyes redden. The Lamp Elder is his master's master; it was he who lent the Qianli caravan its lamp oil ten years ago. The guard steps aside. 'Go in. You're the ones he's been waiting for.'

name: 灭灯窟
Lamps Out Cave
before: 山脚一排窟里，金面刀卫正一盏盏地掐灭香客点的油灯，掐完了还把灯碗收走。香客们跪在窟外哭，说十几年的长明灯，说灭就灭了。刀卫不解释，只是掐，一窟接一窟，掐到最后一窟门口，几个香客手拉手堵在门上：「这一盏，你们不能灭！」

In a row of caves at the foot of the hill, Gold Mask swordsmen are pinching out the oil lamps pilgrims have lit, one after another, and taking away the bowls. The pilgrims kneel outside weeping: lamps that have burned for a decade and more, snuffed just like that. The guards explain nothing, only pinch, cave after cave, until at the last one a few pilgrims link hands across the door: 'Not this one. You can't put this one out!'
after: 刀卫们退了，了账替他们给香客们讲：灯烟熏黑了壁画，一窟的佛十年就熏成了黑脸，师父才下令灭灯。最后那一窟里点的，是千里号的灯，洞主唯独不许灭它。香客们这才散了，有人小声说：「洞主心狠，灯倒留得心软。」

The swordsmen withdraw and Liaozhang explains to the pilgrims for them. Lamp smoke blackens murals; ten years of it turns a whole cave of Buddhas black-faced, which is why his master ordered the lamps out. In that last cave burns the Qianli caravan's lamp, the one lamp the Lord forbids anyone to put out. The pilgrims disperse at last, one murmuring, 'The Lord's hard-hearted, but soft about that lamp.'

name: 师兄坡
Brothers' Slope
before: 坡上站着一排金面骑卫，领头的几个一见了账，面具后面就笑出了声：「了账师弟，讨债讨回来了？」他们原来都是寺里的和尚，跟着师父脱了袈裟当了金面卫。笑归笑，洞主的令还是令，他们横马拦在坡上：「师弟，不打一场，你过不去。」

A row of Gold Mask riders stands on the slope, and at the sight of Liaozhang a few of their leaders laugh behind their masks. 'Little brother Liaozhang! Back from collecting debts?' They were all monks of the temple who took off their robes with their master and became Gold Masks. Laugh as they may, the Lord's order is still the order, and they turn their horses across the slope. 'Little brother, no getting past without a fight.'
after: 师兄们被打下了马，揉着腰哈哈大笑。他们说七年前那一夜，师父在千里窟里站了一宿，天亮出来，把袈裟叠好放在了佛前，「师父说，守窟的守不住窟，不配穿这身衣服」。他们又说灯公快不行了：「去吧，师弟，他手里有样东西，等着交给沙海来的人。」

Knocked off their horses, the brothers rub their backs and roar with laughter. Seven years ago that night, they say, their master stood in the Qianli Cave until dawn, then came out, folded his robe and laid it before the Buddha. 'He said a keeper who can't keep the caves isn't fit to wear it.' And the Lamp Elder is nearly gone, they add. 'Go, little brother. He has something in his hand he's waiting to give to whoever comes from the Sand Sea.'

name: 灯公禅房
The Lamp Elder's Cell
before: 禅房很小，一张草席，一盏灯，灯碗上刻着一个「千」字，火苗只有豆大，十年没熄过。灯公躺在席上，一百零八岁，瘦得像一截枯枝。可禅房外不太平：一伙盗经贼听说灯公手里有一颗「能让人重活一世」的丹，翻墙进了院子，刀已经抵在了门上。

The cell is tiny: a straw mat and a lamp, its bowl carved with the character Qian, its flame the size of a bean, unextinguished for ten years. The Lamp Elder lies on the mat, a hundred and eight years old, thin as a dry twig. But outside is no peace. Sutra thieves have heard the Elder holds a pill 'that lets a man live his life over' and have come over the wall; their knives are already at the door.
after: 盗经贼被赶走，小马贼把王的油添进灯碗，火苗一下子亮了。灯公睁开眼，从枕下摸出一只小木匣，匣里是一张丹方和一颗暗红的丹：转世丹。他炼了一辈子，只成三颗：一颗他自己没舍得吃，一颗给过千里号的账房，账房没要，说「我这一世的劳苦还没完，本事还要留着算账」。「它能洗去一世的劳苦，留下一世的本事，」灯公说，「让走到头的人，从头再走一遍，走得比上回好。」他把匣子交给了了账，又指了指你们。灯油添满了，灯公闭上眼，像是睡着了，再没醒来。

The thieves chased off, the bandit boy pours the King's oil into the lamp bowl and the flame leaps bright. The Lamp Elder opens his eyes and draws from under his pillow a small wooden box holding a recipe and a dark red pill: the Rebirth Pill. A lifetime of refining produced only three. One he couldn't bring himself to take. One he offered to the Qianli caravan's bookkeeper, who refused: 'This life's labour isn't over yet. I need my skills to finish the accounts.' 'It washes away a lifetime's toil and keeps a lifetime's skill,' the Elder says. 'It lets one who has reached the end walk the road again from the beginning, and walk it better.' He gives the box to Liaozhang and nods toward you. The lamp is full. The Elder closes his eyes as if falling asleep, and does not wake.

name: 做旧坊
The Ageing Workshop
before: 一座院子里晾着几百张发黄的经卷，几个抄经生被锁着脚，日夜抄经，抄完了用茶水泡、用烟熏、拿脚踩，做成几百年前的「古经」，卖给关内的收藏家。看院子的是一伙打手，监工拿着一卷真经对照，说「错一个字，剁一根指头」。

Hundreds of yellowed sutra scrolls hang drying in a courtyard. A few copyists, shackled at the ankle, copy sutras day and night; the finished scrolls are soaked in tea, smoked, trodden underfoot and turned into 'ancient sutras' centuries old, to be sold to collectors inside the Pass. Toughs guard the yard, and the overseer checks against a genuine scroll: 'One wrong character, one finger off.'
after: 打手被打跑，抄经生们卸了镣。了账捧着监工那卷「真经」看了半天，说这是藏经洞里被盗出来的。最老的抄经生说，藏经洞里还有一部了不得的经，是千里号三百人那年冬天一人抄一段合成的，「字有好有坏，可一个字都不错」。藏经洞就在河边。

The toughs chased off, the copyists' shackles are struck off. Liaozhang studies the overseer's 'genuine' scroll: it was stolen from the temple's library cave. The oldest copyist says there's a remarkable sutra in the library cave, one the Qianli three hundred copied that winter, a section each, bound into one. 'Good hands and bad, but not one wrong character.' The library cave is down by the river.

name: 藏经洞
The Library Cave
before: 河边的崖脚有一个不起眼的洞口，里头一层套一层，是千佛洞藏经的地方。洞外一片空地，从前是寺里和山外换货的地方：寺里铸钟、修佛要木料，就拿化了的旧铜器跟山外换。如今一伙盗经贼占了洞口，在里面翻箱倒柜，洞外的买卖也全断了。最里面一间黑漆漆的，他们点着火把也看不清，正要放一把火「照个亮」。

At the foot of the cliff by the river is an unremarkable opening, rooms within rooms: the place where the caves keep their scriptures. The open ground outside used to be where the temple traded with the world: it needs timber for casting bells and mending statues, and pays in old bronze melted down. Now sutra thieves hold the entrance and are ransacking the inside, and all trade outside has stopped. The innermost chamber is pitch black; even with torches they can't see, and they're about to light a fire 'for a bit of light'.
after: 盗经贼被赶出了洞，洞外又做起了买卖：木料一车车拉进来，换走寺里的铜。了账掏出那面铜镜，对着洞口的太阳一照，一束光打进最里间，照亮了一整面墙：墙上是用墨写的账，从出关、沙海一路记到这里，每一笔欠了谁、还了谁。最后一段是账房的字：「千佛洞：借灯油三百斤，借经一部，押印一方。诸路之账，至此对毕，独差一车，不知落在何处。此车不清，账不能合。往绿洲王城问。」字写得很重，像是写的人把笔按断了。

The thieves driven out, trade starts again outside: timber comes in by the cartload and goes out as the temple's bronze. Liaozhang takes out the bronze mirror and catches the sun at the entrance, and a beam strikes into the innermost chamber and lights a whole wall. It is covered in accounts in ink, from the Pass through the Sand Sea to here, every debt and to whom and every repayment. The last passage is in the bookkeeper's hand: 'Thousand Buddha Caves: lamp oil borrowed, three hundred jin. One sutra borrowed. One seal pledged. All the road's accounts are reconciled to this point, save one cart, whereabouts unknown. Until this cart is cleared the books will not balance. Inquire at the Oasis King's city.' The strokes are heavy, as if the writer had pressed until the brush broke.

name: 河湾菜园
River Bend Garden
before: 河湾里一片菜园，白菜、韭菜、萝卜一畦畦的，是寺里种了几十年的。一伙兵痞占了园子，在菜地里挖坑烤羊，拿寺里的铜磬当锅，把种菜的老园头赶到河边去挑水，一天挑八十担，挑不够不给饭吃。

A vegetable garden in the river bend, cabbage, chives and radishes bed by bed, tended by the temple for decades. Soldier-thugs have taken it, dug pits in the beds to roast sheep, use the temple's bronze chime bowl as a cooking pot, and send the old gardener to haul water from the river, eighty loads a day or no supper.
after: 兵痞被撵走，老园头扔下扁担，先去看他的韭菜。他说这园子种的菜，有一半是送到灯公禅房的，灯公吃了一辈子素，最爱一碗韭菜面。了账说灯公走了，老园头愣了半天，割了一把最嫩的韭菜，说要送去供上。

The thugs thrown out, the old gardener drops his carrying pole and goes to look at his chives first. Half of what this garden grows goes to the Lamp Elder's cell, he says; the Elder ate vegetarian all his life and loved nothing better than a bowl of noodles with chives. Liaozhang tells him the Elder has passed. The gardener stands frozen a long while, then cuts a handful of the tenderest chives to lay as an offering.
first: 兵痞的营里抄出八只烤了一半的羊、十二坛酒（在菜园里藏酒，老园头直念佛）、一口当锅使的铜磬，还有三车偷来的柴火。

In the thugs' camp you find eight half-roasted sheep, twelve jars of wine (hidden in a temple garden; the gardener mutters prayers), the bronze chime bowl they used as a pot, and three cartloads of stolen firewood.
pass: 每次路过，老园头都从地里拔一筐水灵灵的白菜萝卜，捆一把韭菜，再塞一包晒干的红枣：「灯公留下的规矩，过路的人，菜管够。」

Every time you pass, the old gardener pulls a basket of crisp cabbages and radishes, ties up a bundle of chives and slips in a bag of dried red dates. 'The Lamp Elder's rule: travellers get all the vegetables they want.'

name: 别营沙
Farewell Camp Sands
before: 戈壁上一片空地，地上排着整整齐齐的灶石，三块一组，一组挨一组，一眼望不到头。一伙私盐贩子把这里当成了歇脚的营盘，拿灶石支锅煮盐，还把好几组灶石扒开，说底下准埋着什么。了账说，这是千里号开春离开千佛洞那一夜扎营的地方。

An open patch of gravel desert laid with hearthstones in neat rows, three to a set, set after set, further than you can see. A band of salt smugglers uses it as a rest camp, boiling salt over the hearths, and has pulled several sets apart, sure something must be buried underneath. This, says Liaozhang, is where the Qianli caravan camped the night they left the caves in spring.
after: 私盐贩子被赶走，你们把扒开的灶石摆回原处。每组灶石底下都埋着一只小陶灯，灯碗里还有一层干了的油。了账数了数，一组一灯，三百组。他说那一夜三百人每人点了一盏灯，天亮出发前把灯埋在灶下，「意思是：火还在这儿，人会回来」。

The smugglers chased off, you put the hearthstones back. Beneath every set is buried a small clay lamp with a film of dried oil in its bowl. Liaozhang counts: one lamp to a set, three hundred sets. That night, he says, each of the three hundred lit a lamp, and before setting off at dawn they buried them under the hearths. 'Meaning: the fire stays here, and the people will come back.'

name: 收账营
The Debt Buyers
before: 路边扎着一营关内来的「收账人」，帐篷上挂着幌子：「专收千里号旧账，三折现银」。他们从沙海、从鬼市、从各路人手里低价收来一摞摞千里号的欠条，打算拿着欠条去千佛洞，去千里号三百家的家里，挨家挨户地讨。营里雇了一帮刀手，见了账的和尚袍就骂：「又是个讨债的，抢生意来了！」

A camp of 'debt collectors' from inside the Pass stands by the road under a banner: 'Qianli caravan debts bought. Thirty per cent in silver.' They've bought up stacks of Qianli IOUs cheap from the Sand Sea, the ghost market and everywhere else, and mean to take them to the caves and to the homes of all three hundred families and collect door to door. They've hired swordsmen, who curse at the sight of Liaozhang's robe: 'Another debt collector, come to steal our business!'
after: 刀手们被打散，了账一张张翻那些欠条，翻完了冷笑一声：字迹、印章、日子，没有一张对得上藏经洞墙上的账，「千里号的账，只有我们寺里的和沙海那个王的是真的，账房记的每一笔，我都抄着」。他把一摞假欠条扔进了火里：「这一笔，记在他们自己账上。」

The swordsmen scattered, Liaozhang leafs through the IOUs and, at the end, gives a cold laugh: hand, seal and date, not one matches the accounts on the library cave wall. 'The only genuine Qianli debts are ours at the temple and the King's in the Sand Sea. I've copied every entry the bookkeeper made.' He throws the stack of fakes on the fire. 'That one goes on their own account.'

name: 西去道
The Westward Road
before: 别营沙往外，一条被踩实了的旧路伸进戈壁，路口横着一队金面骑卫。他们不许人往这条路上走，说洞主有令：「千里号走过的路，谁也不许跟。」过路的驼队只好绕远道，多走三天。

Beyond the Farewell Camp, an old trodden road runs out into the gravel desert, and a troop of Gold Mask riders sits across its mouth. No one may set foot on it: the Lord's orders. 'The road the Qianli caravan took is not to be followed by anyone.' Passing camel trains have to go the long way round, three extra days.
after: 骑卫们被打退，领头的说这条令不是洞主自己想出来的，是账房当年托付的：「后面要是有人来找我们，别让他跟。王城的账，我自己去算。」可洞主等了十年，只等来刮脸的、盗经的、冒名的。路边隔一段就有一个小石龛，龛里摆着一盏干了的灯。

The riders beaten back, their leader says the order isn't the Lord's own idea. The bookkeeper asked it of him: 'If anyone comes looking for us, don't let them follow. I'll settle the accounts in the King's city myself.' But in ten years of waiting the Lord has had only face-scrapers, sutra thieves and impostors. At intervals along the roadside stand little stone niches, each holding a dry lamp.

name: 王油窖
The King's Oil Cellar
before: 河边死胡同里有一座凿进崖里的窖，窖门上按着一个歪歪扭扭的「王」字：沙海的王送来的灯油，用不完的都存在这里。一伙河匪摸进了窖，步、弩、骑三路把住窖口，正一坛坛往外搬，准备顺河运出去卖，搬一坛，喊一声「发财」。

Down a dead end by the river is a cellar cut into the cliff, its door pressed with that lopsided character, King: the lamp oil sent by the King of the Sand Sea, and whatever wasn't burned is stored here. River bandits have got in and hold the mouth with foot, crossbow and horse, hauling out jar after jar to ship downriver and sell, shouting 'Rich!' with every jar.
after: 河匪被打退，你们清点窖里的油：一年一排，十排，最早的那排封泥上刻着丁未年秋。了账算了算：千里号欠寺里的三百斤灯油，王第三年就还清了，「后面七年，是他自己要送的」。最边上一坛没开封，坛口贴着纸条：「给账房，回来时点。」

The bandits beaten back, you count the oil: one row a year, ten rows, the earliest seal carved with the autumn of Dingwei. Liaozhang does the sums: the three hundred jin the Qianli caravan owed the temple were paid off by the King's third year. 'The seven years after that, he sent because he wanted to.' The jar at the very end is still sealed, a paper slip on its mouth: 'For the bookkeeper. Light it when he's back.'

name: 三级滩
Three-Step Banks
before: 河两岸是一级一级的台地，像大台阶，一级比一级高。一伙河匪在最低的一级河滩上扎营，靠着水好饮马，四处劫掠。夏天山里的雪化了，河水一天比一天涨，上游已经冲下来浑黄的泥水，他们还在滩上喝酒，笑话你们不敢下来打。

The riverbanks rise in terraces, step above step like a giant staircase. A gang of river bandits camps on the lowest strand, handy for watering their horses, and raids all around. It's summer, the mountain snow is melting and the river is rising day by day; muddy yellow water is already coming down from upstream, and they're drinking on the strand and jeering that you daren't come down and fight.
after: 了账不让你们在低滩扎营：「河边这一级级台地，都是河往下切留下的旧河滩，越高越老，洪水只淹得上最低那一级。」你们在高处守夜，半夜水头下来，河匪的营盘泡进了水里，天亮时被你们一个个捞上岸。千里号也把藏经洞的经搬上了最高一级。

Liaozhang won't let you camp on the low strand. 'These steps along the river are old riverbeds the river left behind as it cut down. The higher, the older, and a flood only reaches the lowest.' You hold the high ground overnight. At midnight the flood crest drowns the bandits' camp, and at dawn you haul them out of the water one by one. The Qianli caravan carried the library cave's sutras up to caves on the highest terrace for the same reason.

name: 押印龛
The Pledged Seal
before: 一座小佛龛里，佛像膝上供着一方铜印，印纽是一只蹲着的骆驼。一伙寻宝的游侠听说这方印是「千里号宝藏的钥匙」，正围着佛龛撬佛像的手指头，想把印拿下来。看龛的老香灯和尚抱着佛像的腿，被拖出去好几丈。

In a small shrine, a bronze seal rests on the Buddha's knees, its handle a crouching camel. A band of treasure-hunting knights-errant has heard the seal is 'the key to the Qianli treasure' and is prising at the statue's fingers to get it out. The old monk who tends the lamps here clings to the statue's leg and has been dragged several yards.
after: 游侠们被打跑，了账拿起铜印往掌心一按，四个字：「千里号账房」。这就是债簿上那一行「账房押印一方，言回程来赎」。了账翻开债簿，在千里号那一页写：「灯油三百斤，王已代还；经一部，借往王城；印一方，在佛前。」写完，他盯着空白处看了很久。

The knights-errant chased off, Liaozhang presses the seal into his palm: 'Qianli Caravan Bookkeeper.' This is the 'one seal pledged, to be redeemed on the way back' in his debt book. He opens the book at the Qianli page and writes: 'Lamp oil, three hundred jin: paid on their behalf by the King. One sutra: borrowed, taken to the King's city. One seal: before the Buddha.' Then he stares at the blank space below for a long time.

name: 三百灯龛
Three Hundred Lamp Niches
before: 西去道两旁的小石龛一个接一个，一直排到戈壁深处，每个龛里一盏干了的灯。一伙流沙匪住在龛群里，拿龛当窝，把灯碗掏出来当酒碗。了账让小马贼把王的灯油卸下来，要沿路把灯一盏盏点上，流沙匪却不让：「点了灯，我们夜里睡不着！」

The little stone niches along the westward road run one after another deep into the gravel desert, each with a dry lamp. A gang of quicksand bandits lives among them, using the niches as dens and the lamp bowls as wine cups. Liaozhang has the bandit boy unload the King's oil to light the lamps one by one along the road, but the bandits won't have it. 'Light them and we won't get any sleep at night!'
after: 流沙匪被赶走，了账一盏一盏添油点灯，你们跟在后面数，一共三百盏。天黑下来，灯火连成一线，一头接着别营沙，一头弯过戈壁，指着东北边一座金光闪闪的山门，再往外才是去绿洲王城的路。了账说：「他们是想让后来的人，夜里也找得着路。」

With the bandits gone, Liaozhang fills and lights the lamps one by one while you follow, counting: three hundred. As dark falls the flames join into a single line, one end at the Farewell Camp, the other curving across the desert toward a gate gleaming gold on the mountain to the north-east, and only beyond it the road to the Oasis King's city. 'They wanted whoever came after to find the way, even at night,' says Liaozhang.

name: 拒徒营
No Disciples Camp
before: 戈壁上一大营金面骑卫，旗子、刀、马都比别处多。领头的一见了账，就把一封信扔到他脚下：「洞主说，了账回寺里念经，不许上山，尤其不许你上。」营里的骑卫和弩手已经列好了阵，看来是专门等他的。

A large camp of Gold Mask riders on the gravel plain, with more banners, blades and horses than anywhere else. Their leader takes one look at Liaozhang and tosses a letter at his feet. 'The Lord says Liaozhang goes back to the temple to chant sutras. He doesn't come up the mountain. You least of all.' The riders and crossbowmen are already drawn up; it seems they've been waiting specially for him.
after: 骑卫们被打退，了账捡起那封信，信上只有一句话：「我已不是你师父，账不必对。」了账把信折好塞进债簿：「师父教我的头一条，就是账一定要对。他不是我师父，也还欠我一个『为什么』。」领头的骑卫低声说：「洞主是怕你看见他现在的样子。」

The riders beaten back, Liaozhang picks up the letter. It holds a single line: 'I am no longer your master. The accounts need not be settled.' He folds it into his debt book. 'The first thing Master taught me was that accounts must always be settled. Even if he isn't my master any more, he still owes me a why.' The lead rider says quietly, 'The Lord doesn't want you to see what he's become.'

name: 灯芯摊
The Wick Stall
before: 路口一个香客摊，卖香、卖蜡、卖灯芯，摊主是个嗓门比铜锣还大的老太婆。金面卫不许香火进窟，她的香卖不出去，一队金面刀卫还天天来查她的灯芯，说怕她偷偷往窟里卖。老太婆抄起擀灯芯的木板，站在摊前骂了半个时辰，没一句重样。

A pilgrims' stall at the crossroads selling incense, candles and lamp wicks, run by an old woman with a voice louder than a gong. The Gold Masks won't allow incense in the caves, so her incense doesn't sell, and a troop of Gold Mask swordsmen comes every day to inspect her wicks in case she's selling them into the caves on the sly. She grabs her wick-rolling board, plants herself before her stall and curses them for half an hour without repeating herself once.
after: 刀卫们被骂退一半、打退一半，老太婆这才开了张，嘴上不饶人，秤上不亏人。她一眼认出了账：「这不是小时候偷我麻糖的小秃子吗！」她说十年来千里号那盏灯的灯芯都是她搓的，驼毛掺棉线，「千里号留下的老骆驼，每年掉的毛都归我」。

Half cursed and half beaten back, the swordsmen withdraw, and the old woman opens for trade, sharp of tongue but honest at the scales. She recognises Liaozhang at once. 'If it isn't the little baldy who used to steal my sesame candy!' For ten years she's rolled the wicks for the Qianli lamp, camel hair twisted with cotton. 'Every bit of fur that old camel the caravan left behind sheds each year comes to me.'

name: 截经道
Sutra Ambush Road
before: 戈壁上一伙盗经贼背着鼓鼓囊囊的包袱往外跑，正撞上你们。领头的怀里揣着一卷经，包得严严实实，跑起来叮当响，是经卷两头的铜轴。他们见了账穿着僧袍，以为是寺里追来的，扔下几个人断后，其余的拼命往沙里钻。

A band of sutra thieves runs out across the desert with bulging bundles and blunders straight into you. Their leader has a scroll clutched to his chest, tightly wrapped and clinking as he runs: the bronze rollers at either end. Seeing Liaozhang's robe they take him for the temple in pursuit, leave a few men to cover them and dive for the dunes.
after: 断后的被打倒，领头那卷经被夺了下来。了账展开一看，是一部经的第一卷，每段末尾都署着一个名字，有工整的，有歪扭的，有的只画了押。卷尾写着：「千里号三百人，丁未冬合抄。」了账直跺脚：「这是千里经！一共十卷，他们全偷走了！」

The rearguard knocked down, you wrest the leader's scroll from him. Liaozhang unrolls it: the first fascicle of a sutra, each section signed with a name, some neat, some crooked, some just a mark. At the end: 'Copied together by the three hundred of the Qianli caravan, winter of Dingwei.' Liaozhang stamps his foot. 'The Qianli Sutra! There are ten fascicles, and they've stolen every one!'

name: 两清坡
Settling Slope
before: 上山的最后一道坡上，金面卫的刀卫、弩手排成三排，个个面具冲着了账。了账却不急了，在坡下支起一张小桌，摆开债簿和砚台，把藏经洞的账、灯公的丹、王的油、佛前的印，一样样摆在桌上。他对坡上喊：「师兄们，等我写完这一笔，再打不迟。」

On the last slope before the mountain, Gold Mask swordsmen and crossbowmen stand in three ranks, every mask turned toward Liaozhang. But Liaozhang is in no hurry now. He sets up a little table at the foot of the slope, lays out his debt book and inkstone, and sets on it one by one the library cave's accounts, the Lamp Elder's pill, the King's oil and the seal from before the Buddha. He calls up the slope: 'Brothers, let me write this one entry, then we can fight.'
after: 坡上的金面卫让开了。了账在千里号那一页写下最后两行：「千里号欠千佛洞：印一方，已赎。千佛洞欠千里号：粥十年，崖一面，路一条，灯三百盏。」他放下笔：「两清了。剩下的，是我师父欠他自己的。」他把债簿合上，抬头看着山门：「我去讨这一笔。」

The Gold Masks on the slope give way. On the Qianli page Liaozhang writes the last two lines: 'Owed by the Qianli caravan to the Thousand Buddha Caves: one seal, now redeemed. Owed by the caves to the Qianli caravan: ten years of porridge, one cliff, one road, three hundred lamps.' He lays down the brush. 'All square. What's left is what my master owes himself.' He closes the book and looks up at the gate. 'I'm going to collect that one.'
